claims.claim: Didymus the Blind was a Christian theologian in the Church of Alexandria, where he taught for about half a century.
Didymus the Blind was born c. 313 and died c. 398.
Didymus became blind at the age of four, before he had learned to read.
Didymus was a student of Origen.
Didymus was a leading opponent of Arianism.
After Didymus' death, he was condemned, along with Origen and Evagrius Ponticus, in connection with the 2nd Council of Constantinople in 553.
Because of this condemnation, most of his works were not copied during the European Middle Ages and thus were lost.
Didymus's Commentary on the Proverbs survives only in fragments preserved in catenae (chain commentaries).
Modern knowledge of Didymus has been greatly increased by papyrus codices discovered in 1941 at a munitions dump near Tura, Egypt, though these do not include the Proverbs commentary.
Didymus's exegesis on Proverbs is important for understanding the history of Alexandrian theology and for characterizing Didymus as a writer.
